newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac urges exporters to seek out new markets.
newsitem.headline: Chirac urges exporters to seek out new markets.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac urged exporters on Wednesday to seek out new markets in Asia and elsewhere and not concentrate solely on Europe, government spokesman Alain Lamassoure said.

Chirac, addressing his message especially to small and medium-sized firms, said exporters should "not concentrate only on Europe (but)...prospect for new markets in other continents," Lamassoure said.

"Our exporters should not be aiming to come home and eat supper each night, which is possible when one goes to Frankfurt or Milan but which is harder when one goes to Peking or Bangkok," Lamassoure quoted Chirac as saying.
France announced a record 1996 trade surplus of 122 billion francs on Tuesday and claimed the surge was proof of the country's economic competitiveness.
The centre-right government predicted the surplus could rise to 135-145 billion francs in 1997.
